निवेशं चक्रिरे सर्वे पुराणां नृवरास्तदा॥ ५॥
verses.m: Hearing the admonition of Kuśa all those four jewels among men, who were the noblest in the world, forthwith laid the foundation of four cities. (5)

verses.text:
कुशाम्बस्तु महातेजाः कौशाम्बीमकरोत् पुरीम्।
कुशनाभस्तु धर्मात्मा पुरं चक्रे महोदयम्॥ ६॥
verses.m: Kuśāmba, who was possessed of exceptional glory, for his part founded the city of Kauśāmbī (named after himself); while Kuśanābha, whose mind was given to piety, built the city named Mahodaya, the modern Kannauja. (6)

verses.text:
असूर्तरजसो नाम धर्मारण्यं महामतिः।
चक्रे पुरवरं राजा वसुनामा गिरिव्रजम्॥ ७॥
verses.m: Asūrtarajasa built a city, Dharmāraṇya by name; while the prince named Vasu built Girivraja, the modern Rajgir, the foremost of all cities. (7)

verses.text:
एषा वसुमती नाम वसोस्तस्य महात्मनः।
एते शैलवराः पञ्च प्रकाशन्ते समन्ततः॥ ८॥
verses.m: This capital of that high-souled prince, Vasu, was also designated after him as Vasumatī. These five great hills* cast their splendour all round the city of Girivraja, justifying the appellation given to it. (8)

verses.text:
सुमागधी नदी रम्या मगधान् विश्रुताऽऽययौ।
पञ्चानां शैलमुख्यानां मध्ये मालेव शोभते॥ ९॥
verses.m: The beautiful and celebrated river Sona, which spreads its charm like a garland in the midst of these five prominent hills flows from the west into the territory of Magadha and is accordingly known as the holy Māgadhī. (9)

verses.text:
सैषा हि मागधी राम वसोस्तस्य महात्मनः।
पूर्वाभिचरिता राम सुक्षेत्रा सस्यमालिनी॥ १०॥
verses.m: This celebrated river Māgadhī, O Rāma, which flows in an easterly direction and is lined with charming fields on both sides and is thus adorned with rows of crops, is connected with the same high-souled Vasu, O Rāma ! (10)

verses.text:
कुशनाभस्तु राजर्षिः कन्याशतमनुत्तमम्।
जनयामास धर्मात्मा घृताच्यां रघुनन्दन॥ ११॥
verses.m: The royal sage Kuśanābha, for his part, whose mind was given to righteousness, O scion of Raghu, begot a hundred daughters, excelled by none, through an Apsarā or celestial nymph named Ghṛtācī. (11)

verses.text:
तास्तु यौवनशालिन्यो रूपवत्यः स्वलंकृताः।
उद्यानभूमिमागम्य प्रावृषीव शतह्रदाः॥ १२॥
गायन्त्यो नृत्यमानाश्च वादयन्त्यस्तु राघव।
आमोदं परमं जग्मुर्वराभरणभूषिताः॥ १३॥
verses.m: With their comeliness enhanced on their attaining maturity, they for their part would repair to the grounds of the royal garden duly adorned with sandal-paste and flowers etc., and decked with excellent jewels and shining like flashes of lighting during the monsoon, and they experienced supreme delight while singing, dancing and playing on their lutes, O scion of Raghu ! (12-13)

verses.text:
अथ ताश्चारुसर्वाङ्ग्यो रूपेणाप्रतिमा भुवि।
उद्यानभूमिमागम्य तारा इव घनान्तरे॥ १४॥
verses.m: Lovely of every limb and peerless on earth in comeliness of form they shone like stars in the midst of clouds on reaching the garden grounds. (14)

verses.text:
ताः सर्वा गुणसम्पन्ना रूपयौवनसंयुताः।
दृष्ट्वा सर्वात्मको वायुरिदं वचनमब्रवीत्॥ १५॥
verses.m: Seeing them all endowed with excellences and rich in beauty and youth, one day the wind-god, who is bodily present everywhere, addressed the following words to them : (15)

verses.text:
अहं वः कामये सर्वा भार्या मम भविष्यथ।
मानुषस्त्यज्यतां भावो दीर्घमायुरवाप्स्यथ॥ १६॥
verses.m: “I wish to have you all as my own. You should, therefore, be my wedded wives. The thought that you are human beings should be given up. In this way you will attain a long lease of life. (16)

verses.text:
चलं हि यौवनं नित्यं मानुषेषु विशेषतः।
अक्षयं यौवनं प्राप्ता अमर्यश्च भविष्यथ॥ १७॥
verses.m: “Indeed youth is ever fleeting, especially in human beings. If you accept me as your husband, you will attain undecaying (abiding) youth and will become immortal.” (17)

verses.text:
तस्य तद् वचनं श्रुत्वा वायोरक्लिष्टकर्मणः।
अपहास्य ततो वाक्यं कन्याशतमथाब्रवीत्॥ १८॥
अन्तश्चरसि भूतानां सर्वेषां सुरसत्तम।
प्रभावज्ञाश्च ते सर्वाः किमर्थमवमन्यसे॥ १९॥
verses.m: Hearing the aforesaid proposal of the celebrated wind-god, whose movements are ever unobstructed, and then deriding his offer, all the hundred damsels presently said, “In the form of life-breath you move inside all living beings, O jewel among gods ! And we are aware of your glory, yet we cherish no attraction for you. Why then do you insult us by making an unseemly offer to us? (18-19)

verses.text:
कुशनाभसुता देव समस्ताः सुरसत्तम।
स्थानाच्च्यावयितुं देवं रक्षामस्तु तपो वयम्॥ २०॥
verses.m: “We are all daughters of Kuśanābha, O god, the foremost of all gods ! We can bring you down from your exalted position by pronouncing a curse on you, yet, even though you are a god, we are anxious to preserve our ascetic glory (which is sure to diminish in the event of our cursing you). (20)

verses.text:
मा भूत् स कालो दुर्मेधः पितरं सत्यवादिनम्।
अवमन्य स्वधर्मेण स्वयं वरमुपास्महे॥ २१॥
verses.m: “Let not that unpropitious hour ever turn up, O evil-minded one, when prompted by lust (our baser nature) we should crave for and accept a match on our own initiative disregarding our veracious father. (21)

verses.text:
पिता हि प्रभुरस्माकं दैवतं परमं च सः।
यस्य नो दास्यति पिता स नो भर्ता भविष्यति॥ २२॥
verses.m: “For father is our master; nay, he is our supreme deity. He alone will be our husband to whom our father will give us away.” (22)

verses.text:
तासां तु वचनं श्रुत्वा हरिः परमकोपनः।
प्रविश्य सर्वगात्राणि बभञ्ज भगवान् प्रभुः॥ २३॥
verses.m: Hearing their insolent and defiant reply, however, the all-pervading wind-god, who is not only glorious and powerful but exceedingly irascible also, entered all their limbs and distorted them. (23)

verses.text:
ताः कन्या वायुना भग्ना विविशुर्नृपतेर्गृहम्।
प्रविश्य च सुसम्भ्रान्ताः सलज्जाः सास्रलोचनाः॥ २४॥
verses.m: Distorted by the wind-god, the aforesaid maidens returned to the king’s (their father’s) palace. Having entered it, they felt much perturbed and abashed and their eyes were filled with tears. (24)

verses.text:
स च ता दयिता भग्नाः कन्याः परमशोभनाः।
दृष्ट्वा दीनास्तदा राजा सम्भ्रान्त इदमब्रवीत्॥ २५॥
verses.m: Perplexed to see those beloved and most charming girls deformed and miserable at that moment, the king (Kuśanābha) asked the following question : (25)

verses.text:
किमिदं कथ्यतां पुत्र्यः को धर्ममवमन्यते।
कुब्जाः केन कृताः सर्वाश्चेष्टन्त्यो नाभिभाषथ।
एवं राजा विनिःश्वस्य समाधिं संदधे ततः॥ २६॥
verses.m: “What is this strange phenomenon? The whole thing may be related to me; who has violated the principles of justice? By whom have you all been turned hunchbacks and how is it that you are all making gestures and do not utter a word?” Making the aforesaid inquiry and heaving a deep sigh, the king then composed himself in order to hear their reply. (26)

verses.text:
तस्य तद् वचनं श्रुत्वा कुशनाभस्य धीमतः।
शिरोभिश्चरणौ स्पृष्ट्वा कन्याशतमभाषत॥ १॥
verses.m: Hearing the aforesaid question of the celebrated and wise Kuśanābha, all the hundred maidens touched his feet with their heads and replied as follows : (1)

verses.text:
वायुः सर्वात्मको राजन् प्रधर्षयितुमिच्छति।
अशुभं मार्गमास्थाय न धर्मं प्रत्यवेक्षते॥ २॥
verses.m: “Resorting to the evil path, the all-pervading wind-god, Your Majesty, sought to violate us and did not respect our righteous conduct. (2)

verses.text:
पितृमत्यः स्म भद्रं ते स्वच्छन्दे न वयं स्थिताः।
पितरं नो वृणीष्व त्वं यदि नो दास्यते तव॥ ३॥
तेन पापानुबन्धेन वचनं न प्रतीच्छता।
एवं ब्रुवन्त्यः सर्वाः स्म वायुनाभिहता भृशम्॥ ४॥
verses.m: “We said to him, ‘May good betide you, we are dependent on our father and as such are not masters of our own will. Ask you us of our father; we shall certainly accept you as our husband if he gives us away to you.’ Pleading thus we were hit hard (deformed) by him of wicked intent, who did not heed our remonstrance.” (3-4)

verses.text:
तासां तु वचनं श्रुत्वा राजा परमधार्मिकः।
प्रत्युवाच महातेजाः कन्याशतमनुत्तमम्॥ ५॥
क्षान्तं क्षमावतां पुत्र्यः कर्तव्यं सुमहत् कृतम्।
ऐकमत्यमुपागम्य कुलं चावेक्षितं मम॥ ६॥
verses.m: “The act of forbearance done by you, which can be done only by those given to forgiveness, my daughters, was extremely noble on your part. And the fact that the honour of my race was vindicated by you by resorting to unanimity on this point was also a unique achievement on your part. (5-6)

verses.text:
अलंकारो हि नारीणां क्षमा तु पुरुषस्य वा।
दुष्करं तच्च वै क्षान्तं त्रिदशेषु विशेषतः॥ ७॥
यादृशी वः क्षमा पुत्र्यः सर्वासामविशेषतः।
क्षमा दानं क्षमा सत्यं क्षमा यज्ञाश्च पुत्रिकाः॥ ८॥
verses.m: “For forbearance is the ornament indeed of womankind as well as of man. And such forbearance particularly with reference to gods as exists in you all without distinction, O my daughters, is difficult to practise. Forbearance is really charity, forbearance is devotion to truth, and forbearance constitutes all sacrifices, my beloved daughters ! (7-8)

verses.text:
क्षमा यशः क्षमा धर्मः क्षमायां विष्ठितं जगत्।
विसृज्य कन्याः काकुत्स्थ राजा त्रिदशविक्रमः॥ ९॥
मन्त्रज्ञो मन्त्रयामास प्रदानं सह मन्त्रिभिः।
देशे काले च कर्तव्यं सदृशे प्रतिपादनम्॥ १०॥
verses.m: (Hearing their complaint, the king, for his part, who was exceedingly pious and exceptionally glorious, replied as follows to his hundred daughters, excelled by none :) “Forbearance is fame, forbearance is piety; nay, the entire creation is established in forbearance, crystallized in the form of the earth.” Having sent away the girls to the gynaeceum, O scion of Kakutstha, the king (Kuśanābha), who possessed the prowess of gods and was adept in deliberation, discussed the question of their marriage with his counsellors since it was necessary to give them away to a worthy man at the proper place and time. (9-10)

verses.text:
एतस्मिन्नेव काले तु चूली नाम महाद्युतिः।
ऊर्ध्वरेताः शुभाचारो ब्राह्मं तप उपागमत्॥ ११॥
verses.m: At this very time a Brahmacārī (lit., one who has turned the flow of his generative fluid upwards and never allowed it to escape), Cūlī by name, who was exceptionally glorious and given to virtuous conduct, actually embarked upon a course of austerities* (in the form of meditation) directed towards the realization of Brahmā. (11)

verses.text:
तपस्यन्तमृषिं तत्र गन्धर्वी पर्युपासते।
सोमदा नाम भद्रं ते ऊर्मिलातनया तदा॥ १२॥
verses.m: At that very place, during the period of his askesis, may good betide you, a Gandharva girl, Somadā by name, daughter of Ūrmilā, waited upon the Ṛṣi in the hope of securing his goodwill, while he was busy practising his austerities. (12)

verses.text:
सा च तं प्रणता भूत्वा शुश्रूषणपरायणा।
उवास काले धर्मिष्ठा तस्यास्तुटोऽभवद् गुरुः॥ १३॥
verses.m: Bending low before him and devoted to his service, that most pious girl waited upon him at the right time whenever her presence was needed by him. The venerable sage got pleased with her. (13)

verses.text:
स च तां कालयोगेन प्रोवाच रघुनन्दन।
परितुष्टोऽस्मि भद्रं ते किं करोमि तव प्रियम्॥ १४॥
verses.m: And when the propitious hour came, the sage, O scion of Raghu, said to the girl, ‘I am highly pleased with your innocent services, may all be well with you ! What service can I do to you?’ (14)

verses.text:
परितुष्टं मुनिं ज्ञात्वा गन्धर्वी मधुरस्वरम्।
उवाच परमप्रीता वाक्यज्ञा वाक्यकोविदम्॥ १५॥
verses.m: Supremely delighted to know the sage much gratified, the eloquent Gandharva girl spoke as follows in a sweet voice to the seer, who was a master of speech : (15)

verses.text:
लक्ष्म्या समुदितो ब्राह्म्या ब्रह्मभूतो महातपाः।
ब्राह्मेण तपसा युक्तं पुत्रमिच्छामि धार्मिकम्॥ १६॥
verses.m: “A great ascetic illumined with Brahmic (spiritual) splendour, you have become one with the Infinite. Hence I seek from you a pious son, rich in askesis (in the form of meditation) directed towards the realization of Brahma, the Absolute. (16)

verses.text:
अपतिश्चास्मि भद्रं ते भार्या चास्मि न कस्यचित्।
ब्राह्मेणोपगतायाश्च दातुमर्हसि मे सुतम्॥ १७॥
verses.m: “As for myself, I am unmarried nor shall I be the wife of any. Therefore, let your grace descend on me. Be pleased to grant me a son by dint of your Brahmic (spiritual) glory, since I have sought refuge in you.” (17)

verses.text:
तस्याः प्रसन्नो ब्रह्मर्षिर्ददौ ब्राह्ममनुत्तमम्।
ब्रह्मदत्त इति ख्यातं मानसं चूलिनः सुतम्॥ १८॥
verses.m: Full of delight, the Brāhmaṇa sage Cūlina (a variant of Cūlī) conferred on her a mind-born son, rich in askesis (in the form of meditation) directed towards the realization of Brahma, excelled by none and known by the name of ‘Brahmadatta’. (18)

verses.text:
स राजा ब्रह्मदत्तस्तु पुरीमध्यवसत् तदा।
काम्पिल्यां परया लक्ष्म्या देवराजो यथा दिवम्॥ १९॥
verses.m: Invested with supreme (royal) splendour, the said Brahmadatta for his part lived at that time as king in the city of Kāmpilyā (built by Kampila) as Indra (the ruler of gods) does in paradise. (19)

verses.text:
स बुद्धिं कृतवान् राजा कुशनाभः सुधार्मिकः।
ब्रह्मदत्ताय काकुत्स्थ दातुं कन्याशतं तदा॥ २०॥
verses.m: The aforesaid Kuśanābha, a most pious king, at that time made up his mind, O scion of Kakutstha, to give away all his hundred daughters to Brahmadatta. (20)

verses.text:
तमाहूय महातेजा ब्रह्मदत्तं महीपतिः।
ददौ कन्याशतं राजा सुप्रीतेनान्तरात्मना॥ २१॥
verses.m: Calling the said Brahmadatta, the exceptionally glorious king (Kuśanābha), the ruler of the earth, gave away with a most cheerful mind all the hundred girls to him. (21)

verses.text:
यथाक्रमं तदा पाणिं जग्राह रघुनन्दन।
ब्रह्मदत्तो महीपालस्तासां देवपतिर्यथा॥ २२॥
verses.m: At the time of marriage, O scion of Raghu, King Brahmadatta, who shone like Indra (the ruler of gods), married them one after another by taking their hands in his in order of seniority. (22)

verses.text:
स्पृष्टमात्रे तदा पाणौ विकुब्जा विगतज्वराः।
युक्तं परमया लक्ष्म्या बभौ कन्याशतं तदा॥ २३॥
verses.m: The moment their hands were touched by Brahmadatta in the course of the wedding, the girls got cured of their deformity and were rid of their agony. Invested with supreme splendour all the hundred girls shone brightly at that time. (23)

verses.text:
स दृष्ट्वा वायुना मुक्ताः कुशनाभो महीपतिः।
बभूव परमप्रीतो हर्षं लेभे पुनः पुनः॥ २४॥
verses.m: King Kuśanābha was highly pleased to see them freed from morbid affection of the windy humour in their body and experienced joy again and again. (24)

verses.text:
कृतोद्वाहं तु राजानं ब्रह्मदत्तं महीपतिम्।
सदारं प्रेषयामास सोपाध्यायगणं तदा॥ २५॥
verses.m: King Kuśanābha then sent away King Brahmadatta, the delighter of his subjects, alongwith his wedded wives and the host of his family-priests, as soon as he was actually married. (25)

verses.text:
सोमदापि सुतं दृष्ट्वा पुत्रस्य सदृशीं क्रियाम्।
यथान्यायं च गन्धर्वो स्नुषास्ताः प्रत्यनन्दत।
स्पृष्ट्वा स्पृष्ट्वा च ताः कन्याः कुशनाभं प्रशस्य च॥ २६॥
verses.m: Seeing the union of her son worthy of her, Somadā, the Gandharva damsel, too joyfully greeted her son as well as her aforesaid daughters-in-law, one after another, in order of seniority and, embracing the said brides again and again and applauding Kuśanābha for his hospitality and rich dowry, she departed from there. (26)

verses.text:
कृतोद्वाहे गते तस्मिन् ब्रह्मदत्ते च राघव।
अपुत्रः पुत्रलाभाय पौत्रीमिष्टिमकल्पयत्॥ १॥
verses.m: The aforesaid Brahmadatta having left after being married, O scion of Raghu, Kuśanābha, who had no male issue, embarked upon a sacrifice intended to procure a son with the object of securing a male issue. (1)

verses.text:
इष्ट्यां तु वर्तमानायां कुशनाभं महीपतिम्।
उवाच परमोदारः कुशो ब्रह्मसुतस्तदा॥ २॥
verses.m: In the meantime, while the sacrifice was actually going on, the highly magnanimous Kuśa, the father of Kuśanābha and son of Brahmā (the creator) prophesied to King Kuśanābha as follows : (2)

verses.text:
पुत्रस्ते सदृशः पुत्र भविष्यति सुधार्मिकः।
गाधिं प्राप्स्यसि तेन त्वं कीर्तिं लोके च शाश्वतीम्॥ ३॥
verses.m: “ ‘A most pious son, worthy of you, will be born to you, my son! You will have Gādhi for your son and thereby attain undying glory in the world.’ (3)

verses.text:
एवमुक्त्वा कुशो राम कुशनाभं महीपतिम्।
जगामाकाशमाविश्य ब्रह्मलोकं सनातनम्॥ ४॥
verses.m: “Informing King Kuśanābha accordingly, O Rāma, Kuśa withdrew to the immortal Satyaloka (the realm of Brahmā, from which he had obviously come), coursing through the airspace. (4)

verses.text:
कस्यचित् त्वथ कालस्य कुशनाभस्य धीमतः।
जज्ञे परमधर्मिष्ठो गाधिरित्येव नामतः॥ ५॥
verses.m: “After sometime indeed a most pious son, Gādhi by name, the very name given by Kuśa, was born to the wise Kuśanābha. (5)

verses.text:
स पिता मम काकुत्स्थ गाधिः परमधार्मिकः।
कुशवंशप्रसूतोऽस्मि कौशिको रघुनन्दन॥ ६॥
verses.m: “That exceedingly pious man, Gādhi by name, was my father, O descendant of Kakutstha ! And descended in the line of Kuśa, I am known as Kauśika, O scion of Raghu ! (6)

verses.text:
पूर्वजा भगिनी चापि मम राघव सुव्रता।
नाम्ना सत्यवती नाम ऋचीके प्रतिपादिता॥ ७॥
verses.m: “I had an elder sister too, of noble vows, known by the name of Satyavatī and given away to the sage, Ṛcīka. (7)

verses.text:
सशरीरा गता स्वर्गं भर्तारमनुवर्तिनी।
कौशिकी परमोदारा प्रवृत्ता च महानदी॥ ८॥
दिव्या पुण्योदका रम्या हिमवन्तमुपाश्रिता।
लोकस्य हितकार्यार्थं प्रवृत्ता भगिनी मम॥ ९॥
verses.m: “Following as she did, the wishes of her husband throughout her life, my sister bodily ascended to heaven and later on turned into a most beneficent and delightful great river—Kauśikī (the modern Kosi), flowing by the side of the Himalayas, unearthly in character, whose waters confer merit on those using it—and is thus engaged in doing good to the world. (8-9)

verses.text:
ततोऽहं हिमवत्पार्श्वे वसामि नियतः सुखम्।
भगिन्यां स्नेहसंयुक्तः कौशिक्यां रघुनन्दन॥ १०॥
verses.m: “Full of affection for my sister, I had been happily leading a life of self-discipline since then by the side of the Himalayas on the banks of the Kauśikī, O scion of Raghu ! (10)

verses.text:
सा तु सत्यवती पुण्या सत्ये धर्मे प्रतिष्ठिता।
पतिव्रता महाभागा कौशिकी सरितां वरा॥ ११॥
verses.m: “That pious and highly blessed lady, Satyavatī, who was established in the virtue of truthfulness and exclusively devoted to her husband, is still extant in the form of Kauśikī, the foremost of rivers. (11)

verses.text:
अहं हि नियमाद् राम हित्वा तां समुपागतः।
सिद्धाश्रममनुप्राप्तः सिद्धोऽस्मि तव तेजसा॥ १२॥
verses.m: “Leaving that river I came down to the plains because of my vow to perform a sacrifice at some consecrated spot and arrived at Siddhāśrama, where I got accomplished of my purpose by dint of your glory (might). (12)

verses.text:
एषा राम ममोत्पत्तिः स्वस्य वंशस्य कीर्तिता।
देशस्य हि महाबाहो यन्मां त्वं परिपृच्छसि॥ १३॥
verses.m: “In this way has been told by me my birth from the loins of Gādhi, the genesis of my race (from Kuśa, son of Brahmā) and the history of the land of Girivraja extending along the bank of the Sona, which you asked me in particular, O mighty-armed Rāma ! (13)

verses.text:
गतोऽर्धरात्रः काकुत्स्थ कथाः कथयतो मम।
निद्रामभ्येहि भद्रं ते मा भूद् विघ्नोऽध्वनीह नः॥ १४॥
verses.m: “Half of the night has passed in my narrating past episodes, O scion of Kakutstha ! Peace be with you ! Now go to sleep. Let there be no interference in this journey of ours due to torpor caused by sleeplessness. (14)

verses.text:
निष्पन्दास्तरवः सर्वे निलीना मृगपक्षिणः।
नैशेन तमसा व्याप्ता दिशश्च रघुनन्दन॥ १५॥
verses.m: “All the trees are motionless, the beasts and birds are buried in sleep and the quarters stand enveloped in the darkness of night, O scion of Raghu ! (15)

verses.text:
शनैर्विसृज्यते संध्या नभा नेत्रैरिवावृतम्।
नक्षत्रतारागहनं ज्योतिर्भिरवभासते॥ १६॥
verses.m: “The evening twilight has gradually receded and the firmament, thick set with lunar mansions and other stars, is shinning with the heavenly bodies as though covered with innumerable eyes. (16)

verses.text:
उत्तिष्ठते च शीतांशुः शशी लोकतमोनुदः।
ह्लादयन् प्राणिनां लोके मनांसि प्रभया स्वया॥ १७॥
verses.m: “The moon, which dispels the darkness of the world at night, is just rising*, diffusing its cool rays and delighting the minds of all living beings in the world by its soothing and refreshing splendour. (17)

verses.text:
नैशानि सर्वभूतानि प्रचरन्ति ततस्ततः।
यक्षराक्षससंघाश्च रौद्राश्च पिशिताशनाः॥ १८॥
verses.m: “All nocturnal beings, viz., fearful hosts of Yakṣas and Rākṣasas as well as fiends (feeding on raw flesh) are freely roaming here and there.” (18)

verses.text:
एवमुक्त्वा महातेजा विरराम महामुनिः।
साधु साध्विति ते सर्वे मुनयो ह्यभ्यपूजयन्॥ १९॥
verses.m: Saying so, the exceptionally glorious and great sage Viśwāmitra, became silent and all the aforesaid sages, who accompanied him, applauded him saying “Well spoken ! Good !! (19)

verses.text:
कुशिकानामयं वंशो महान् धर्मपरः सदा।
ब्रह्मोपमा महात्मानः कुशवंश्या नरोत्तमाः॥ २०॥
verses.m: “Great is this race of Kuśa and ever given to righteousness too. The high-souled kings descended in the line of Kuśa have been as good as Brāhmaṇa Ṛṣis. (20)

verses.text:
विशेषेण भवानेव विश्वामित्र महायशः।
कौशिकी सरितां श्रेष्ठा कुलोद्द्योतकरी तव॥ २१॥
verses.m: “You, O highly illustrious Viśwāmitra, who have attained Brahmanhood by dint of your austerities, are particularly so. And Kauśikī, the foremost of rivers, has added to the lustre of your race.” (21)

verses.text:
मुदितैर्मुनिशार्दूलैः प्रशस्तः कुशिकात्मजः।
निद्रामुपागमच्छ्रीमानस्तंगत इवांशुमान्॥ २२॥
verses.m: Extolled thus by the foremost of sages, who were full of delight, the glorious Viśwāmitra, the son of Gādhi, a scion of Kuśa, fell asleep even as the sun sinks below the horizon. (22)

verses.text:
रामोऽपि सहसौमित्रिः किंचिदागतविस्मयः।
प्रशस्य मुनिशार्दूलं निद्रां समुपसेवते॥ २३॥
verses.m: Glorifying Viśwāmitra, a tiger among sages, Śrī Rāma too, who felt a bit amazed to hear the family history of Viśwāmitra, courted sleep alongwith Lakṣmaṇa, son of Sumitrā. (23)

verses.text:
उपास्य रात्रिशेषं तु शोणाकूले महर्षिभिः।
निशायां सुप्रभातायां विश्वामित्रोऽभ्यभाषत॥ १॥
verses.m: Having reposed for the rest of the night on the bank of the Sona alongwith the great Ṛṣis, who accompanied him on the journey, Viśwāmitra spoke as follows on the night having culminated in a beautiful sunrise : (1)

verses.text:
सुप्रभाता निशा राम पूर्वा संध्या प्रवर्तते।
उत्तिष्ठोत्तिष्ठ भद्रं ते गमनायाभिरोचय॥ २॥
verses.m: “The night has ended in a lovely dawn, O Rāma ! The morning twilight has set in. Get up, arise and make yourself ready to proceed further. May happiness and well-being attend you !” (2)

verses.text:
तच्छ्रुत्वा वचनं तस्य कृतपूर्वाह्णिकक्रियः।
गमनं रोचयामास वाक्यं चेदमुवाच ह॥ ३॥
verses.m: Hearing his instruction as aforesaid and having finished his morning duties (Sandhyā etc.,) Śrī Rāma made himself ready to leave for the journey and spoke the following words: so the tradition goes : (3)

verses.text:
अयं शोणः शुभजलोगाधः पुलिनमण्डितः।
कतरेण पथा ब्रह्मन् संतरिष्यामहे वयम्॥ ४॥
verses.m: “The river Sona, whose waters are so holy, is fordable here and as such adorned with sandy banks. By which of the two fords (appearing before us) shall we wade through it, O holy Sir?” (4)

verses.text:
एवमुक्तस्तु रामेण विश्वामित्रोऽब्रवीदिदम्।
एष पन्था मयोद्दिष्टो येन यान्ति महर्षयः॥ ५॥
verses.m: Questioned thus by Śrī Rāma, Viśwāmitra indeed replied as follows : “Here is the ford already pointed out by me, through which the great Ṛṣis over there are wading.” (5)

verses.text:
एवमुक्ता महर्षयो विश्वामित्रेण धीमता।
पश्यन्तस्ते प्रयाता वै वनानि विविधानि च॥ ६॥
verses.m: After wise Viśwāmitra said so, the Maharṣis enjoying the beautiful sceneries of the forest departed. (6)

verses.text:
ते गत्वा दूरमध्वानं गतेऽर्धदिवसे तदा।
जाह्नवीं सरितां श्रेष्ठां ददृशुर्मुनिसेविताम्॥ ७॥
verses.m: Then having crossed the Sona at the spot mentioned by Viśwāmitra and traversed a long way further, the party sighted the Gaṅgā, the foremost of all rivers, resorted to by sages, in the afternoon. (7)

verses.text:
तां दृष्ट्वा पुण्यसलिलां हंससारससेविताम्।
बभूवुर्मुनयः सर्वे मुदिताः सहराघवाः॥ ८॥
तस्यास्तीरे तदा सर्वे चक्रुर्वासपरिग्रहम्।
ततः स्नात्वा यथान्यायं संतर्प्य पितृदेवताः॥ ९॥
verses.m: The sages, including Śrī Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa, the two scions of Raghu, were all rejoiced to see the celebrated river, whose waters confer merit (on those who resort to them) and which was frequented by swans and cranes. (8-9)

verses.text:
हुत्वा चैवाग्निहोत्राणि प्राश्य चामृतवद्धविः।
विविशुर्जाह्नवीतीरे शुभा मुदितमानसाः॥ १०॥
विश्वामित्रं महात्मानं परिवार्य समन्ततः।
विष्ठिताश्च यथान्यायं राघवौ च यथार्हतः।
सम्प्रहृष्टमना रामो विश्वामित्रमथाब्रवीत्॥ ११॥
verses.m: On the bank of that river all of them forthwith broke their journey. Having then bathed in the river according to the scriptural ordinance, (i.e., after reciting a Vedic hymn known as the Aghamarṣaṇa-Sūkta—vide Ṛgveda X. 190), duly propitiated the manes and gods (including Ṛṣis) with libations of water and also poured oblations into the sacred fire and partaken of the remnants of the sacrifice, which have been likened* to ambrosia in the Śāstras, the blessed Ṛṣis sat down on the bank of the Gaṅgā with a cheerful mind surrounding the high-souled Viśwāmitra on all sides. When they were all comfortably seated in order of seniority as also Śrī Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa (the two scions of Raghu) according to their position, Śrī Rāma presently addressed Viśwāmitra as follows with an overjoyed mind : (10-11)

verses.text:
भगवञ्छ्रोतुमिच्छामि गङ्गां त्रिपथगां नदीम्।
त्रैलोक्यं कथमाक्रम्य गता नदनदीपतिम्॥ १२॥
verses.m: “I wish to hear, O venerable Sir, about the holy river Gaṅgā, which takes a threefold course, flowing as it does through heaven, the earth and the subterranean regions, how having coursed through the three worlds, viz., heaven and earth and the space intervening the two, it meets the ocean (the ruler of rivers, both big and small).” (12)

verses.text:
चोदितो रामवाक्येन विश्वामित्रो महामुनिः।
वृद्धिं जन्म च गङ्गाया वक्तुमेवोपचक्रमे॥ १३॥
verses.m: Impelled by the inquiry of Śrī Rāma, the great sage Viśwāmitra started discoursing on the origin as well as on the expansion of the holy Gaṅgā, as follows : (13)

verses.text:
शैलेन्द्रो हिमवान् राम धातूनामाकरो महान्।
तस्य कन्याद्वयं राम रूपेणाप्रतिमं भुवि॥ १४॥
verses.m: “There stands (on the extreme north of India) O Rāma, the great Himālaya, the king of mountains and a storehouse of minerals. A couple of daughters, matchless in beauty on earth, were born to the deity presiding over the said mountain, O Rāma ! (14)

verses.text:
या मेरुदुहिता राम तयोर्माता सुमध्यमा।
नाम्ना मेना मनोज्ञा वै पत्नी हिमवतः प्रिया॥ १५॥
verses.m: “The charming and beloved consort of Himavān, the deity presiding over the Himālayas, Menā by name, who was marked by a slender waist and was the daughter of Mount Meru, was their mother, O Rāma ! (15)

verses.text:
तस्यां गङ्गेयमभवज्ज्येष्ठा हिमवतः सुता।
उमा नाम द्वितीयाभूत् कन्या तस्यैव राघव॥ १६॥
verses.m: “The elder daughter of Himavān, born through her, was this Gaṅgā. A second daughter, Umā by name, was born to the selfsame Himavān, O scion of Raghu ! (16)

verses.text:
अथ ज्येष्ठां सुराः सर्वे देवकार्यचिकीर्षया।
शैलेन्द्रं वरयामासुर्गङ्गां त्रिपथगां नदीम्॥ १७॥
verses.m: “With the intention of accomplishing through her the purpose of gods, all the gods presently asked Himavān, the king of mountains, for the elder of the two, viz., Gaṅgā, who later turned into a river that follows a threefold course. (17)

verses.text:
ददौ धर्मेण हिमवांस्तनयां लोकपावनीम्।
स्वच्छन्दपथगां गङ्गां त्रैलोक्यहितकाम्यया॥ १८॥
verses.m: “From considerations of piety (according to which the solicitation of a supplicant is not to be rejected) and out of solicitude for the welfare of the three worlds, Himavān gave in adoption to gods his daughter, Gaṅgā, who is capable of purifying the world and who could carve her way even through the airspace and the subterranean regions according to her own free will. (18)

verses.text:
प्रतिगृह्य त्रिलोकार्थं त्रिलोकहितकाङ्क्षिणः।
गङ्गामादाय तेऽगच्छन् कृतार्थेनान्तरात्मना॥ १९॥
verses.m: “Accepting the gift so readily given by the pious Himavān in the interest of the three worlds and taking the Gaṅgā with them, the gods, who wished well of the three worlds, left with their mind fully satisfied. (19)

verses.text:
या चान्या शैलदुहिता कन्याऽऽसीद् रघुनन्दन।
उग्रं सुव्रतमास्थाय तपस्तेपे तपोधना॥ २०॥
verses.m: “The other daughter of Himavān, who looked upon askesis as Her only wealth, O scion of Raghu, practised austerities in the shape of meditation on Lord Śiva, while remaining a virgin and observing a noble and formidable vow of forgoing even dry leaves to keep Her body and soul together. (20)

verses.text:
उग्रेण तपसा युक्तां ददौ शैलवरः सुताम्।
रुद्रायाप्रतिरूपायं उमां लोकनमस्कृताम्॥ २१॥
verses.m: “Himavān, the chief of mountains, gave away to Lord Rudra (the god of destruction), who has no rival, this daughter, Umā who was rich in severe asceticism and adored by the universe. (21)

verses.text:
एते ते शैलराजस्य सुते लोकनमस्कृते।
गङ्गा च सरितां श्रेष्ठा उमा देवी च राघव॥ २२॥
verses.m: “Gaṅgā, the foremost of rivers, and Goddess Umā, these are the two well-known daughters of Himavān, the king of mountains, who are venerated by the whole universe, O scion of Raghu ! (22)

verses.text:
एतत् ते सर्वमाख्यातं यथा त्रिपथगामिनी।
खं गता प्रथमं तात गतिं गतिमतां वर॥ २३॥
सैषा सुरनदी रम्या शैलेन्द्रतनया तदा।
सुरलोकं समारूढा विपापा जलवाहिनी॥ २४॥
verses.m: “In this way everything connected with the origin of Gaṅgā has been narrated to you. Now hear how it followed a threefold course. In the first place (as I have told you in verse 18 above), O dear Rāma, it rose into the sky, which allows moving space to all mobile beings alongwith the gods who took her away to heaven. Then this celebrated daughter of Himavān, the king of mountains, rose to heaven (the realm of gods) in the form of the delightful Mandākinī, the heavenly stream visible in the form of the milky way, and last of all assumed the form of an earthly stream, Gaṅgā, capable of ridding the world of its sins.” (23-24)

verses.text:
उक्तवाक्ये मुनौ तस्मिन्नुभौ राघवलक्ष्मणौ।
प्रतिनन्द्य कथां वीरावूचतुर्मुनिपुंगवम्॥ १॥
verses.m: The aforesaid sage, Viśwāmitra, having concluded his speech, both the heroes, Śrī Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa, hailed with joy the story of the two daughters of Himavān, told by him and spoke as follows to Viśwāmitra, the foremost of sages : (1)

verses.text:
धर्मयुक्तमिदं ब्रह्मन् कथितं परमं त्वया।
दुहितुः शैलराजस्य ज्येष्ठाया वक्तुमर्हसि।
विस्तरं विस्तरज्ञोऽसि दिव्यमानुषसम्भवम्॥ २॥
verses.m: “You have narrated, holy Sir, this most excellent story capable of conferring merit on those who hear it. Be pleased now to give a detailed account of Gaṅgā (the elder daughter of Himavān), relating to her celestial and earthly career, since you know these details. (2)

verses.text:
त्रीन् पथो हेतुना केन प्लावयेल्लोकपावनी।
कथं गङ्गा त्रिपथगा विश्रुता सरिदुत्तमा॥ ३॥
verses.m: “With what motive did that world-purifying stream choose to wash all the three regions (heaven, earth and the space intervening them)? How did the Gaṅgā, which takes a threefold course, come to be known as the foremost of rivers? (3)

verses.text:
त्रिषु लोकेषु धर्मज्ञ कर्मभिः कैः समन्विता।
तथा ब्रुवति काकुत्स्थे विश्वामित्रस्तपोधनः॥ ४॥
निखिलेन कथां सर्वामृषिमध्ये न्यवेदयत्।
पुरा राम कृतोद्वाहः शितिकण्ठो महातपाः।
दृष्ट्वा च भगवान् देवीं मैथुनायोपचक्रमे॥ ५॥
तस्य संक्रीडमानस्य महादेवस्य धीमतः।
शितिकण्ठस्य देवस्य दिव्यं वर्षशतं गतम्॥ ६॥
verses.m: “With what achievements is she associated in the three worlds, O knower of Dharma (what is right)?” While Śrī Rāma (a scion of Kakutstha) was speaking thus, Viśwāmitra, who claims askesis as his only wealth, narrated in extenso in the midst of the Ṛṣis, that accompanied him, the whole story as follows : “Seeing Goddess Pārvatī by His side, O Rāma, Lord Śiva, who bears a blue patch on His throat, nay, who is noted for His great asceticism and had just married Her, devoted Himself to the delights of conjugal bliss. A hundred celestial years (equivalent to 36,000 human years) rolled past the all-wise Lord Śiva, the Supreme Deity, while He sported with His Spouse. (4—6)

verses.text:
न चापि तनयो राम तस्यामासीत् परंतप।
सर्वे देवाः समुद्युक्ताः पितामहपुरोगमाः॥ ७॥
यदिहोत्पद्यते भूतं कस्तत् प्रतिसहिष्यति।
अभिगम्य सुराः सर्वे प्रणिपत्येदमब्रुवन्॥ ८॥
देवदेव महादेव लोकस्यास्य हिते रत।
सुराणां प्रणिपातेन प्रसादं कर्तुमर्हसि॥ ९॥
verses.m: “Neither any son nor any daughter was, however, born of Her, O Rāma, the chastiser of foes ! All the gods with Brahmā, the progenitor of the entire creation, as their leader girded up their loins to stop the amorous sport. For, they said to themselves, ‘Who will be able to bear the glory of the offspring that is born of this divine Lady?’ Approaching Him and falling prostrate before Him, all the gods addressed to Him the following prayer : ‘O Supreme Lord, the adored of all gods, devoted as You are to the good of this universe, be pleased to extend Your grace to us, gods, in response to our prostrations. (7—9)

verses.text:
न लोका धारयिष्यन्ति तव तेजः सुरोत्तम।
ब्राह्मेण तपसा युक्तो देव्या सह तपश्चर॥ १०॥
verses.m: “ ‘The worlds or their denizens will not be able to bear Your glory in the shape of Your progeny, O Chief of gods ! Therefore, rich as You are in askesis in the form of oneness with Brahma, desist from enjoying the delights of connubial bliss and practise austerities alongwith Your Divine Consort. (10)

verses.text:
त्रैलोक्यहितकामार्थं तेजस्तेजसि धारय।
रक्ष सर्वानिमाँल्लोकान् नालोकं कर्तुमर्हसि॥ ११॥
verses.m: “ ‘For the welfare of all the three worlds, which is Your chief concern, pray retain Your vital energy in Your own glorious Self and thereby preserve all these worlds from destruction, for the son that will be born to You will be extremely glorious and will burn all the three worlds. Pray, do not bring about the extinction of the worlds.’ (11)

verses.text:
देवतानां वचः श्रुत्वा सर्वलोकमहेश्वरः।
बाढमित्यब्रवीत् सर्वान् पुनश्चेदमुवाच ह॥ १२॥
धारयिष्याम्यहं तेजस्तेजसैव सहोमया।
त्रिदशाः पृथिवी चैव निर्वाणमधिगच्छतु॥ १३॥
verses.m: “Hearing the remonstrance of the gods, Lord Śiva (the suzerain Lord of all the worlds) said ‘Amen !’ And further addressed the following words to them all, so the tradition goes : ‘I alongwith Umā shall retain Our vital energy by dint of Our very glory (retentive power). Let the terrestrial globe as also the other worlds, O gods, live in peace, i.e., free from fear of destruction. (12-13)

verses.text:
यदिदं क्षुभितं स्थानान्मम तेजो ह्यनुत्तमम्।
धारयिष्यति कस्तन्मे ब्रुवन्तु सुरसत्तमाः॥ १४॥
verses.m: “But who shall receive that vital fluid of Mine, unsurpassed as it is, which is already shaken from its seat in the heart? Tell Me this, O jewels among gods !” (14)

verses.text:
एवमुक्तास्ततो देवाः प्रत्यूचुर्वृषभध्वजम्।
यत्तेजः क्षुभितं ह्यद्य तद् धरा धारयिष्यति॥ १५॥
verses.m: Questioned thus by Lord Śiva, the gods thereupon replied to Lord Śiva (whose ensign bears the device of a bull), ‘Earth (who is capable of holding everything) will indeed receive the vital fluid that has got dislodged so far.’ (15)

verses.text:
एवमुक्तः सुरपतिः प्रमुमोच महाबलः।
तेजसा पृथिवी येन व्याप्ता सगिरिकानना॥ १६॥
verses.m: Addressed thus by the gods, the almighty Lord Śiva, the Ruler of gods, let fall His seed, by which was covered the entire globe including the mountains and forests. (16)

verses.text:
ततो देवाः पुनरिदमूचुश्चापि हुताशनम्।
आविश त्वं महातेजो रौद्रं वायुसमन्वितः॥ १७॥
verses.m: Thereupon fearing lest the earth may be cracked by being covered all over by the powerful fluid, the gods further addressed the following prayer to the god of fire that feeds on the sacrificial offerings : ‘Accompanied by the wind-god (and mobilized by him) suck you the mighty seed of Rudra (the god of destruction).’ (17)

verses.text:
तदग्निना पुनर्व्याप्तं संजातं श्वेतपर्वतम्।
दिव्यं शरवणं चैव पावकादित्यसंनिभम्॥ १८॥
यत्र जातो महातेजाः कार्तिकेयोऽग्निसम्भवः।
अथोमां च शिवं चैव देवाः सर्षिगणास्तथा॥ १९॥
पूजयामासुरत्यर्थं सुप्रीतमनसस्तदा।
अथ शैलसुता राम त्रिदशानिदमब्रवीत्॥ २०॥
समन्युरशपत् सर्वान् क्रोधसंरक्तलोचना।
यस्मान्निवारिता चाहं संगता पुत्रकाम्यया॥ २१॥
अपत्यं स्वेषु दारेषु नोत्पादयितुमर्हथ।
अद्यप्रभृति युष्माकमप्रजाः सन्तु पत्नयः॥ २२॥
verses.m: Concentrated by fire (assisted by the wind-god), it now got consolidated into a white mountain and was subsequently transformed into a thicket of white reeds resplendent as fire and the sun, in which was born the exceptionally glorious Kārtikeya (so-called because he was suckled later on by the deities presiding over the group of stars known by the name of Kṛttikās), who is accordingly spoken of as fire-born. “Highly delighted in mind on that occasion, the gods including the hosts of Ṛṣis that accompanied them, now profusely worshipped Umā and, even so, Lord Śiva. Thereupon Umā, Daughter of Himavān, with eyes bloodshot through anger pronounced an imprecation on all gods and angrily addressed them as follows : ‘Since I, who was united with My Spouse with the desire of getting a son, have been deterred from the act by you, you shall no longer be able to beget an offspring through your respective consorts. Let your wives remain issueless from this day.’ (18—22)

verses.text:
एवमुक्त्वा सुरान् सर्वान् शशाप पृथिवीमपि।
अवने नैकरूपा त्वं बहुभार्या भविष्यसि॥ २३॥
verses.m: Having addressed all the gods as aforesaid, she cursed Earth, too, in the following words : ‘You will have a multiform surface, O earth, and shall have many masters. (23)

verses.text:
न च पुत्रकृतां प्रीतिं मत्क्रोधकलुषीकृता।
प्राप्स्यसि त्वं सुदुर्मेधो मम पुत्रमनिच्छती॥ २४॥
verses.m: ‘Agitated by My curse, nor shall you enjoy the delight of having a son,* O highly evil-minded lady, since you do not wish that I should have a son.’ (24)

verses.text:
तान् सर्वान् पीडितान् दृष्ट्वा सुरान् सुरपतिस्तदा।
गमनायोपचक्राम दिशं वरुणपालिताम्॥ २५॥
verses.m: Seeing all those gods tormented by the curse of His Spouse, Lord Śiva (the Ruler of gods) prepared to proceed in a westerly direction, the quarter ruled over by Varuṇa, the god of water. (25)

verses.text:
स गत्वा तप आतिष्ठत् पार्श्वे तस्योत्तरे गिरेः।
हिमवत्प्रभवे शृङ्गे सह देव्या महेश्वरः॥ २६॥
verses.m: Going there the celebrated Lord Śiva, the supreme Divinity, took to asceticism alongwith His Consort, Goddess Pārvatī, on the summit called Himavatprabhava in the northern wing of the celebrated mountain, Himālaya.” (26)

verses.text:
एष ते विस्तरो राम शैलपुत्र्या निवेदितः।
गङ्गायाः प्रभवं चैव शृणु मे सहलक्ष्मण॥ २७॥
verses.m: In this way have I told you, O Rāma, a detailed account of Goddess Umā, Daughter of Himavān. Now hear from me alongwith Lakṣmaṇa the story of the origin of the Gaṅgā too. (27)

verses.text:
तप्यमाने तदा देवे सेन्द्राः साग्निपुरोगमाः।
सेनापतिमभीप्सन्तः पितामहमुपागमन्॥ १॥
verses.m: “At that time, while the divinity, Lord Śiva was busy practising austerities alongwith His Consort, Goddess Umā, the gods alongwith Indra (their ruler) and accompanied by the god of fire as their leader approached Brahmā, the progenitor of the entire creation, seeking to secure a commander for their forces. (1)

verses.text:
ततोऽब्रुवन् सुराः सर्वे भगवन्तं पितामहम्।
प्रणिपत्य सुरा राम सेन्द्राः साग्निपुरोगमाः॥ २॥
verses.m: “Falling prostrate before him, all the gods including Indra and accompanied by the god of fire as their leader thereupon addressed the venerable Brahmā as follows, O Rāma (the delighter of gods) : (2)

verses.text:
येन सेनापतिर्देव दत्तो भगवता पुरा।
स तपः परमास्थाय तप्यते स्म सहोमया॥ ३॥
verses.m: “ ‘Resorting to supreme asceticism, the almighty Lord Śiva, O glorious one, by whom a commander for our forces was vouchsafed in the form of seed some time back is practising austerities alongwith Goddess Umā, His Consort. (3)

verses.text:
यदत्रानन्तरं कार्यं लोकानां हितकाम्यया।
संविधत्स्व विधानज्ञ त्वं हि नः परमा गतिः॥ ४॥
verses.m: “ ‘Pray, accomplish what should be done next in this connection with the intention of doing good to the worlds, O knower of expedients, since you are our supreme resort.’ (4)

verses.text:
देवतानां वचः श्रुत्वा सर्वलोकपितामहः।
सान्त्वयन् मधुरैर्वाक्यैस्त्रिदशानिदमब्रवीत्॥ ५॥
verses.m: “Hearing the submission of the gods, Brahmā, the progenitor of the whole universe, addressed the following words to the gods, comforting them with sweet assurances. (5)

verses.text:
शैलपुत्र्या यदुक्तं तन्न प्रजाः स्वासु पत्निषु।
तस्या वचनमक्लिष्टं सत्यमेव न संशयः॥ ६॥
verses.m: “ ‘What has been uttered by Goddess Pārvatī, the daughter of Himavān, viz., that you will have no progeny through your wives must be true: there is no doubt about it; for, Her imprecation is unobstructed. (6)

verses.text:
इयमाकाशगङ्गा च यस्यां पुत्रं हुताशनः।
जनयिष्यति देवानां सेनापतिमरिंदमम्॥ ७॥
verses.m: “ ‘Here is the heavenly Gaṅgā, through whom the god of fire will, by placing in her the seed of Lord Śiva, cause to be born a son capable of subduing his enemies, who will turn out to be the commander of the celestial armies. (7)

verses.text:
ज्येष्ठा शैलेन्द्रदुहिता मानयिष्यति तं सुतम्।
उमायास्तद्बहुमतं भविष्यति न संशयः॥ ८॥
verses.m: “ ‘Gaṅgā, the elder daughter of the king of mountains, will account him as her own son and that belief of hers will be made much of even by Umā, her younger sister: there is no doubt about it.’ (8)

verses.text:
तच्छ्रुत्वा वचनं तस्य कृतार्था रघुनन्दन।
प्रणिपत्य सुराः सर्वे पितामहमपूजयन्॥ ९॥
verses.m: “Satisfied to hear the above reply of Brahmā and falling prostrate before him, O scion of Raghu, all the gods venerated him. (9)

verses.text:
ते गत्वा परमं राम कैलासं धातुमण्डितम्।
अग्निं नियोजयामासुः पुत्रार्थं सर्वदेवताः॥ १०॥
verses.m: “Reaching the most excellent Kailāsa, rich in minerals, O Rāma, all the divinities urged the god of fire to produce a son fit to command the celestial armies. (10)

verses.text:
देवकार्यमिदं देव समाधत्स्व हुताशन।
शैलपुत्र्यां महातेजो गङ्गायां तेज उत्सृज॥ ११॥
verses.m: “They said to him, ‘Accomplish this object of gods, O exceptionally glorious god of fire ! Place in Gaṅgā, the daughter of Himavān, the seed of Lord Śiva borne by you.’ (11)

verses.text:
देवतानां प्रतिज्ञाय गङ्गामभ्येत्य पावकः।
गर्भं धारय वै देवि देवतानामिदं प्रियम्॥ १२॥
verses.m: “Making a promise to the gods to accomplish their aforesaid purpose and, approaching the heavenly Gaṅgā, the god of fire prayed to her as follows : ‘Pray, place in yourself the seed of Lord Śiva, captured and retained by me; for such is the pleasure of gods.’ (12)

verses.text:
इत्येतद् वचनं श्रुत्वा दिव्यं रूपमधारयत्।
स तस्या महिमां दृष्ट्वा समन्तादवशीर्यत॥ १३॥
verses.m: “Hearing the aforesaid request of the god of fire, the celestial river assumed an ethereal living form. Beholding her exquisiteness of form, the seed of Lord Śiva melted on all sides. (13)

verses.text:
समन्ततस्तदा देवीमभ्यषिञ्चत पावकः।
सर्वस्रोतांसि पूर्णानि गङ्गाया रघुनन्दन॥ १४॥
verses.m: “The god of fire then impregnated her on all sides in such a way that all her veins were saturated with the seed, O scion of Raghu ! (14)

verses.text:
तमुवाच ततो गङ्गा सर्वदेवपुरोगमम्।
अशक्ता धारणे देव तेजस्तव समुद्धतम्॥ १५॥
दह्यमानाग्निना तेन सम्प्रव्यथितचेतना।
अथाब्रवीदिदं गङ्गां सर्वदेवहुताशनः॥ १६॥
verses.m: “Burning with that fiery seed and with her mind extremely agonized, Gaṅgā thereupon spoke as follows to the celebrated god of fire, the leader of all the gods : ‘I am unable, O shining one, to bear the seed of Lord Śiva, intensified by thine own.’ The god of fire, who consumes the offerings intended for all gods, made the following reply to Gaṅgā : (15-16)

verses.text:
इह हैमवते पार्श्वे गर्भोऽयं संनिवेश्यताम्।
श्रुत्वा त्वग्निवचो गङ्गा तं गर्भमतिभास्वरम्॥ १७॥
उत्ससर्ज महातेजाः स्रोतोभ्यो हि तदानघ।
यदस्या निर्गतं तस्मात् तप्तजाम्बूनदप्रभम्॥ १८॥
verses.m: “ ‘This seed may kindly be discharged on this offshoot of the Himālayas.’ Hearing the aforesaid suggestion of the god of fire, the exceptionally glorious Gaṅgā for her part expelled from her veins that very moment that most resplendent seed, O sinless Rāma ! Since it emerged from the body of Gaṅgā, a grand-daughter of Sumeru, a mountain of gold, it shone accordingly as molten gold of the purest type. (17-18)

verses.text:
काञ्चनं धरणीं प्राप्तं हिरण्यमतुलप्रभम्।
ताम्रं कार्ष्णायसं चैव तैक्ष्ण्यादेवाभिजायत॥ १९॥
verses.m: “Its residue that fell on earth turned into gold and silver of matchless splendour. Due to the very severity of its heat even distant areas were converted into copper and iron. (19)

verses.text:
मलं तस्याभवत् तत्र त्रपु सीसकमेव च।
तदेतद् धरणीं प्राप्य नानाधातुरवर्धत॥ २०॥
verses.m: “Its dross turned into tin and lead on the earth. In this way on reaching the earth the seed (of Lord Śiva) grew to be various metals. (20)

verses.text:
निक्षिप्तमात्रे गर्भे तु तेजोभिरभिरञ्जितम्।
सर्वं पर्वतसंनद्ध सौवर्णमभवद् वनम्॥ २१॥
verses.m: “The moment the seed was deposited on earth, really speaking the entire thicket of white reeds referred to (in verse 18 of Canto XXXVI) above, alongwith the white mountain was irradiated with its splendour and turned into gold. (21)

verses.text:
जातरूपमिति ख्यातं तदाप्रभृति राघव।
सुवर्णं पुरुषव्याघ्र हुताशनसमप्रभम्।
तृणवृक्षलतागुल्मं सर्वं भवति काञ्चनम्॥ २२॥
verses.m: “From that time onward, O scion of Raghu, gold, which shines like fire, came to be known as Jātarūpa, because it was at that time that its splendid form was brought to light, O tiger among men! and the grass, the creeper plants, the trees and the Gulma—all turned into gold by the contact of that seed. (22)

verses.text:
तं कुमारं ततो जातं सेन्द्राः सहमरुद्गणाः।
क्षीरसम्भावनार्थाय कृत्तिकाः समयोजयन्॥ २३॥
verses.m: “Thereupon the hosts of gods alongwith Indra, their ruler, brought together the boy thus born as well as the Kṛttikās (the female deities presiding over the group of six stars forming the constellation of that name) in a body for the purpose of suckling the babe. (23)

verses.text:
ताः क्षीरं जातमात्रस्य कृत्वा समयमुत्तमम्।
ददुः पुत्रोऽयमस्माकं सर्वासामिति निश्चिताः॥ २४॥
verses.m: “Having arrived at a sublime understanding that the babe in question would be the son of them all and determined accordingly, they (synchronously) suckled the boy as soon as he was born. (24)

verses.text:
ततस्तु देवताः सर्वाः कार्तिकेय इति ब्रुवन्।
पुत्रस्त्रैलोक्यविख्यातो भविष्यति न संशयः॥ २५॥
verses.m: “Thereupon all the gods said, ‘The boy will be celebrated in all the three worlds (heaven, earth and the space intervening them) as a son of the Kṛttikās : there is no doubt about it.’ (25)

verses.text:
तेषां तद् वचनं श्रुत्वा स्कन्नं गर्भपरिस्रवे।
स्नापयन् परया लक्ष्म्या दीप्यमानं यथानलम्॥ २६॥
verses.m: “Hearing the aforesaid utterance of the gods which was so agreeable to them, the Kṛttikās bathed the babe that had first trickled down in the form of seed from the body of Lord Śiva and again on its oozing from the womb of Gaṅgā shone with supreme effulgence like fire. (26)

verses.text:
स्कन्द इत्यब्रुवन् देवाः स्कन्नं गर्भपरिस्रवे।
कार्तिकेयं महाबाहुं काकुत्स्थ ज्वलनोपमम्॥ २७॥
verses.m: “The gods named the mighty-armed son of the Kṛttikās, who was effulgent as fire, O scion of Kakutstha, as Skanda (from the root ‘Skand’—to flow) because he had slipped from the womb of Gaṅgā. (27)

verses.text:
प्रादुर्भूतं ततः क्षीरं कृत्तिकानामनुत्तमम्।
षण्णां षडाननो भूत्वा जग्राह स्तनजं पयः॥ २८॥
गृहीत्वा क्षीरमेकाह्ना सुकुमारवपुस्तदा।
अजयत् स्वेन वीर्येण दैत्यसैन्यगणान् विभुः॥ २९॥
सुरसेनागणपतिमभ्यषिञ्चन् महाद्युतिम्।
ततस्तममराः सर्वे समेत्याग्निपुरोगमाः॥ ३०॥
verses.m: “Then there appeared milk, excelled by no other milk, in the breasts of the Kṛttikās, and growing six-faced, the babe sucked the milk flowing from the breasts of all the six together. Having sucked their milk only for a day the boy, though tender of body, grew so powerful even then that he gradually conquered by sheer dint of his might several divisions of the demon army. Meeting together all the gods, headed by the god of fire, then installed with due ceremony that exceptionally glorious boy as the commander of the celestial forces. (28—30)

verses.text:
एष ते राम गङ्गायां विस्तरोऽभिहितो मया।
कुमारसम्भवश्चैव धन्यः पुण्यस्तथैव च॥ ३१॥
verses.m: “In this way has been told by me, O Rāma, a detailed narrative of the Gaṅgā as also the story of the advent of Kumāra (son of Lord Śiva), which confers wealth as well as religious merit (on the hearer as well as on the reader). (31)

verses.text:
भक्तश्च यः कार्तिकेये काकुत्स्थ भुवि मानवः।
आयुष्मान् पुत्रपौत्रैश्च स्कन्दसालोक्यतां व्रजेत्॥ ३२॥
verses.m: “Nay, a man on earth who is devoted to Kārtikeya, O scion of Kakutstha, bids fair to attain longevity and an abode in the divine realm of Skanda alongwith his sons and grandsons.” (32)

verses.text:
तां कथां कौशिको रामे निवेद्य मधुराक्षराम्।
पुनरेवापरं वाक्यं काकुत्स्थमिदमब्रवीत्॥ १॥
verses.m: Having narrated to Śrī Rāma in sweet accents the aforesaid story, Viśwāmitra, a scion of Kuśa, further related the following other narrative to the scion of Kakutstha. (1)

verses.text:
अयोध्याधिपतिर्वीर पूर्वमासीन्नराधिपः।
सगरो नाम धर्मात्मा प्रजाकामः स चाप्रजः॥ २॥
verses.m: “In the days of old, O heroic Rāma, there was a king, Sagara by name, who ruled over Ayodhyā, and whose mind was given to piety. And being issueless he longed for progeny. (2)

verses.text:
वैदर्भदुहिता राम केशिनी नाम नामतः।
ज्येष्ठा सगरपत्नी सा धर्मिष्ठा सत्यवादिनी॥ ३॥
verses.m: “A daughter of the king of Vidarbha, known by the name of Keśinī, O Rāma, was the eldest wife of Sagara. She was extremely pious and truthful. (3)

verses.text:
अरिष्टनेमेर्दुहिता सुपर्णभगिनी तु सा।
द्वितीया सगरस्यासीत् पत्नी सुमतिसंज्ञिता॥ ४॥
verses.m: “The second wife of Sagara was named as Sumati. She was really speaking a daughter of the sage Ariṣṭanemi (nicknamed Kaśyapa) and a sister of Suparṇa (another name of Garuḍa, the king of birds and the carrier of Lord Viṣṇu). (4)

verses.text:
ताभ्यां सह महाराजः पत्नीभ्यां तप्तवांस्तपः।
हिमवन्तं समासाद्य भृगुप्रस्रवणे गिरौ॥ ५॥
verses.m: “Having reached the Himālaya mountain, the great king practised asceticism on an offshoot of the Himālayas, Bhṛgu-Prasravaṇa by name, alongwith his aforesaid two wives. (5)

verses.text:
अथ वर्षशते पूर्णे तपसाऽऽराधितो मुनिः।
सगराय वरं प्रादाद् भृगुः सत्यवतां वरः॥ ६॥
verses.m: “Propitiated by his askesis, the sage Bhṛgu (a mind-born son of Brahmā), the foremost of the votaries of truth, conferred a boon on Sagara when a hundred years had been completed. (6)

verses.text:
अपत्यलाभः सुमहान् भविष्यति तवानघ।
कीर्तिं चाप्रतिमां लोके प्राप्स्यसे पुरुषर्षभ॥ ७॥
verses.m: “He said, ‘good many sons will be born to you, O sinless one, and you will attain unequalled fame in the world, O jewel among men ! (7)

verses.text:
एका जनयिता तात पुत्रं वंशकरं तव।
षष्टिं पुत्रसहस्राणि अपरा जनयिष्यति॥ ८॥
verses.m: “ ‘One wife of yours will bear you a son that will perpetuate your race, O dear one; while the other will give birth to sixty thousand sons.’ (8)

verses.text:
भाषमाणं महात्मानं राजपुत्र्यौ प्रसाद्य तम्।
ऊचतुः परमप्रीते कृताञ्जलिपुटे तदा॥ ९॥
verses.m: “Propitiating that exalted soul, the sage Bhṛgu, while he was speaking as aforesaid, the two princesses, the daughters of the king of Vidarbha and the sage Kaśyapa, a king of sages, respectively, who were supremely delighted to hear of the boon granted by him, submitted on that occasion with folded hands as follows : (9)

verses.text:
एकः कस्याः सुतो ब्रह्मन् का बहूञ्जनयिष्यति।
श्रोतुमिच्छावहे ब्रह्मन् सत्यमस्तु वचस्तव॥ १०॥
verses.m: “We wish to hear by which of us will be borne a single son and which, O holy one, will give birth to many. Let your prediction be true, O sage !” (10)

verses.text:
तयोस्तद् वचनं श्रुत्वा भृगुः परमधार्मिकः।
उवाच परमां वाणीं स्वच्छन्दोऽत्र विधीयताम्॥ ११॥
verses.m: “Hearing that question of theirs, the supremely pious Bhṛgu gave the following excellent reply : ‘Let your own will be enforced in this matter. (11)

verses.text:
एको वंशकरो वास्तु बहवो वा महाबलाः।
कीर्तिमन्तो महोत्साहाः का वा कं वरमिच्छति॥ १२॥
verses.m: “ ‘In one case there will be a single son that will perpetuate the race and in the other many mighty and renowned sons full of great daring. Which of you would have which boon?’ (12)

verses.text:
मुनेस्तु वचनं श्रुत्वा केशिनी रघुनन्दन।
पुत्रं वंशकरं राम जग्राह नृपसंनिधौ॥ १३॥
verses.m: “Hearing the sage’s reply, Keśinī, the senior queen, for her part, O scion of Raghu, preferred in the presence of the king a son that would perpetuate the line, O Rāma. (13)

verses.text:
षष्टिं पुत्रसहस्राणि सुपर्णभगिनी तदा।
महोत्साहान् कीर्तिमतो जग्राह सुमतिः सुतान्॥ १४॥
verses.m: “Thereupon Sumati, Garuḍa’s sister, sought sixty thousand renowned sons full of great daring. (14)

verses.text:
प्रदक्षिणमृषिं कृत्वा शिरसाभिप्रणम्य तम्।
जगाम स्वपुरं राजा सभार्यो रघुनन्दन॥ १५॥
verses.m: “Going round the sage clockwise and saluting him with his head bent low, the king returned to his capital with his wives, O Rāma ! (15)

verses.text:
अथ काले गते तस्य ज्येष्ठा पुत्रं व्यजायत।
असमञ्ज इति ख्यातं केशिनी सगरात्मजम्॥ १६॥
verses.m: “Now, when the time was ripe, the senior queen, Keśinī, bore Sagara a son, known by the name of Asamañja, sprung from his loins. (16)

verses.text:
सुमतिस्तु नरव्याघ्र गर्भतुम्बं व्यजायत।
षष्टिः पुत्रसहस्राणि तुम्बभेदाद् विनिस्सृताः॥ १७॥
verses.m: “Sumati, on the other hand, O tiger among men, brought forth a foetus shaped like a bitter gourd. On the gourd being split up sixty thousand male issues emerged from it. (17)

verses.text:
घृतपूर्णेषु कुम्भेषु धात्र्यस्तान् समवर्धयन्।
कालेन महता सर्वे यौवनं प्रतिपेदिरे॥ १८॥
verses.m: “The nurses nurtured them placing them in jars full of ghee. After a considerable period of time all attained maturity. (18)

verses.text:
अथ दीर्घेण कालेन रूपयौवनशालिनः।
षष्टिः पुत्रसहस्राणि सगरस्याभवंस्तदा॥ १९॥
verses.m: “Then after a long time sixty thousand sons endowed with comeliness and youthful vigour now stood by the side of King Sagara. (19)

verses.text:
स च ज्येष्ठो नरश्रेष्ठ सगरस्यात्मसम्भवः।
बालान् गृहीत्वा तु जले सरय्वा रघुनन्दन॥ २०॥
प्रक्षिप्य प्राहसन्नित्यं मज्जतस्तान् निरीक्ष्य वै।
एवं पापसमाचारः सज्जनप्रतिबाधकः॥ २१॥
पौराणामहिते युक्तः पित्रा निर्वासितः पुरात्।
तस्य पुत्रोंऽशुमान् नाम असमञ्जस्य वीर्यवान्॥ २२॥
सम्मतः सर्वलोकस्य सर्वस्यापि प्रियंवदः।
ततः कालेन महता मतिः समभिजायत।
सगरस्य नरश्रेष्ठ यजेयमिति निश्चिता॥ २३॥
स कृत्वा निश्चयं राजा सोपाध्यायगणस्तदा।
यज्ञकर्मणि वेदज्ञो यष्टुं समुपचक्रमे॥ २४॥
verses.m: “The aforesaid eldest son of Sagara, however, O jewel among men, actually caught hold of infants, O scion of Raghu, everyday and, throwing them into the waters of the Sarayū, openly and heartily laughed to see them drowning. Thus given to sinful conduct and tormenting pious men and intent on doing harm to the citizens, the youth was exiled by his father from the capital. The valiant son of the aforesaid Asamañja, Aṁśumān by name, on the other hand, was beloved of all people and spoke kindly to all. Then after a considerable period of time a firm resolve was made by Sagara that he should perform a sacrifice, O jewel among men ! Having resolved upon a sacrificial performance, the aforesaid king, who was well-versed in the Vedas, made ready that very moment to undertake a sacrifice alongwith the help of his family-priests.” (20—24)

verses.text:
विश्वामित्रवचः श्रुत्वा कथान्ते रघुनन्दनः।
उवाच परमप्रीतो मुनिं दीप्तमिवानलम्॥ १॥
verses.m: Śrī Rāma, a scion of Raghu, felt supremely delighted to hear the speech of Viśwāmitra. At the end of the discourse he spoke as follows, to the sage who shone as fire : (1)

verses.text:
श्रोतुमिच्छामि भद्रं ते विस्तरेण कथामिमाम्।
पूर्वजो मे कथं ब्रह्मन् यज्ञं वै समुपाहरत्॥ २॥
verses.m: “May God bless you, I wish to hear this story at length. How did my forefather, King Sagara, perform the sacrifice, O holy one?” (2)

verses.text:
तस्य तद् वचनं श्रुत्वा कौतूहलसमन्वितः।
विश्वामित्रस्तु काकुत्स्थमुवाच प्रहसन्निव॥ ३॥
verses.m: Seized with wonder to hear that question of Śrī Rāma, Viśwāmitra for his part replied to the scion of Kakutstha as follows as though laughing heartily : (3)

verses.text:
श्रूयतां विस्तरो राम सगरस्य महात्मनः।
शंकरश्वशुरो नाम्ना हिमवानिति विश्रुतः॥ ४॥
विन्ध्यपर्वतमासाद्य निरीक्षेते परस्परम्।
तयोर्मध्ये समभवद् यज्ञः स पुरुषोत्तम॥ ५॥
verses.m: “Hear, O Rāma, a detailed account of the sacrificial performance of the high-souled Sagara. The father-in-law of Lord Śaṅkara, widely known by the name of Himavān, and the Vindhya mountain gaze on one another, Himavān overlooking Vindhya and vice versa. The aforesaid sacrifice took place in the region lying between the two ranges, O chief of men ! (4-5)

verses.text:
स हि देशो नरव्याघ्र प्रशस्तो यज्ञकर्मणि।
तस्याश्वचर्या काकुत्स्थ दृढधन्वा महारथः॥ ६॥
अंशुमानकरोत् तात सगरस्य मते स्थितः।
तस्य पर्वणि तं यज्ञं यजमानस्य वासवः॥ ७॥
राक्षसीं तनुमास्थाय यज्ञियाश्वमपाहरत्।
ह्रियमाणे तु काकुत्स्थ तस्मिन्नश्वे महात्मनः॥ ८॥
उपाध्यायगणाः सर्वे यजमानमथाब्रुवन्।
अयं पर्वणि वेगेन यज्ञियाश्वोऽपनीयते॥ ९॥
हर्तारं जहि काकुत्स्थ हयश्चैवोपनीयताम्।
यज्ञच्छिद्रं भवत्येतत् सर्वेषामशिवाय नः॥ १०॥
verses.m: “That land,* O tiger among men, is really commended for a sacrificial performance. Remaining at Sagara’s beck and call, O dear Rāma (a scion of Kakutstha), Aṁśumān, a great car-warrior, who was armed with a strong bow played the role of attending the sacrificial horse during its wanderings as its guard. Assuming the semblance of an ogre Indra stole away the sacrificial horse of Sagara, while he was busy performing the said sacrifice on the day of Ukthya (a liturgical ceremony). While the aforesaid horse of the high-souled Sagara was actually being taken away, all the priests officiating at the sacrifice forthwith addressed the sacrificer as follows : ‘On the day of Ukthya, the sacrificial horse is being taken away with vehemence over there. Kill the thief, O scion of Kakutstha, and let the horse be recovered. This obstruction in the sacrificial performance is calculated to bring ill-luck to us all. (6—10)

verses.text:
तत् तथा क्रियतां राजन् यज्ञोऽच्छिद्रः कृतो भवेत्।
सोपाध्यायवचः श्रुत्वा तस्मिन् सदसि पार्थिवः॥ ११॥
षष्टिं पुत्रसहस्राणि वाक्यमेतदुवाच ह।
गतिं पुत्रा न पश्यामि रक्षसां पुरुषर्षभाः॥ १२॥
मन्त्रपूतैर्महाभागैरास्थितो हि महाक्रतुः।
तद् गच्छथ विचिन्वध्वं पुत्रका भद्रमस्तु वः॥ १३॥
verses.m: ‘Therefore, it may be so arranged, O king, that the sacrificial performance is cleared of this impediment.’ Hearing the report of the priests including the family-priest, gathered in that assembly, the king addressed the following words to his sixty thousand sons: so the tradition goes : “I do not perceive, my sons, even the access of ogres to this sacrificial performance, O jewels among men, since this great sacrifice is presided over by highly blessed souls consecrated by the recitation of holy texts. Therefore, go and track out the thief, my beloved sons; may good luck attend you all. (11—13)

verses.text:
समुद्रमालिनीं सर्वां पृथिवीमनुगच्छथ।
एकैकं योजनं पुत्रा विस्तारमभिगच्छत॥ १४॥
verses.m: ‘Ransack the entire globe encircled by the oceans. Apportion to yourselves, my sons, land with an area of one square Yojana (64 sq. miles) each and scour it. (14)

verses.text:
यावत् तुरगसंदर्शस्तावत् खनत मेदिनीम्।
तमेव हयहर्तारं मार्गमाणा ममाज्ञया॥ १५॥
verses.m: ‘If, however, you fail to trace him on the earth’s surface, excavate the earth under my order, looking about for the very individual who has stolen away the horse, till the horse is found. (15)

verses.text:
दीक्षितः पौत्रसहितः सोपाध्यायगणस्त्वहम्।
इह स्थास्यामि भद्रं वो यावत् तुरगदर्शनम्॥ १६॥
verses.m: ‘I for my part, who stand consecrated, will stay here alongwith my grandson, Aṁśumān, and the priests officiating at the sacrifice till the horse is in sight; may good betide you.’ (16)

verses.text:
ते सर्वे हृष्टमनसो राजपुत्रा महाबलाः।
जग्मुर्महीतलं राम पितुर्वचनयन्त्रिताः॥ १७॥
verses.m: “Bound by the words of their father, all those very mighty princes traversed the earth’s surface with a delighted mind, O Rāma ! (17)

verses.text:
गत्वा तु पृथिवीं सर्वामदृष्ट्वा तं महाबलाः।
योजनायामविस्तारमेकैको धरणीतलम्।
बिभिदुः पुरुषव्याघ्रा वज्रस्पर्शसमैर्भुजैः॥ १८॥
verses.m: “Traversing the whole earth and yet not finding the horse, the mighty princes, who were tigers among men, started excavating the earth with their arms whose impact was as hard as that of a thunderbolt, each digging land covering an area of one square Yojana or sixty-four square miles. (18)

verses.text:
शूलैरशनिकल्पैश्च हलैश्चापि सुदारुणैः।
भिद्यमाना वसुमती ननाद रघुनन्दन॥ १९॥
verses.m: “The earth groaned even as it was being dug with pikes hard as adamant as well as with most formidable ploughshares, O scion of Raghu ! (19)

verses.text:
नागानां वध्यमानानामसुराणां च राघव।
राक्षसानां दुराधर्षः सत्त्वानां निनदोऽभवत्॥ २०॥
verses.m: “There was a loud roar, that could not be easily repressed, of Nāgas, demons, ogres and other living beings inhabiting the subterranean regions, that were being killed in the course of the excavation. (20)

verses.text:
योजनानां सहस्राणि षष्टिं तु रघुनन्दन।
बिभिदुर्धरणीं राम रसातलमनुत्तमम्॥ २१॥
verses.m: “They excavated, O scion of Raghu, land covering an area of sixty thousand square Yojanas as if to reach Rasātala (the sixth or penultimate subterranean sphere), a region excelled by no other sphere in point of beauty, splendour and amenities of life, O Rāma ! (21)

verses.text:
एवं पर्वतसम्बाधं जम्बूद्वीपं नृपात्मजाः।
खनन्तो नृपशार्दूल सर्वतः परिचक्रमुः॥ २२॥
verses.m: “In this way, O tiger among princes, the sixty thousand sons of Sagara went about excavating in all directions the land of Jambūdwīpa, thick with mountains. (22)

verses.text:
ततो देवाः सगन्धर्वाः सासुराः सहपन्नगाः।
सम्भ्रान्तमनसः सर्वे पितामहमुपागमन्॥ २३॥
verses.m: “Agitated in mind, gods including Gandharvas, demons and Nāgas, all sought the presence of Brahmā, the progenitor of the entire creation. (23)

verses.text:
ते प्रसाद्य महात्मानं विषण्णवदनास्तदा।
ऊचुः परमसंत्रस्ताः पितामहमिदं वचः॥ २४॥
verses.m: “Glorifying the high-souled Brahmā on that occasion, they made the following submission to him with a doleful face, greatly alarmed as they were : (24)

verses.text:
भगवन् पृथिवी सर्वा खन्यते सगरात्मजैः।
बहवश्च महात्मानो वध्यन्ते जलचारिणः॥ २५॥
verses.m: “ ‘O Lord, the entire globe is being excavated and many exalted souls and aquatic animals killed in the process by the sons of Sagara. (25)

verses.text:
अयं यज्ञहनोऽस्माकमनेनाश्वोऽपनीयते।
इति ते सर्वभूतानि हिंसन्ति सगरात्मजाः॥ २६॥
verses.m: “ ‘The aforesaid sons of Sagara are destroying all created beings suspecting that whosoever comes before them has interfered with their sacrificial performance and that the sacrificial horse has been taken away by him.’ (26)

verses.text:
देवतानां वचः श्रुत्वा भगवान् वै पितामहः।
प्रत्युवाच सुसंत्रस्तान् कृतान्तबलमोहितान्॥ १॥
verses.m: “Hearing the representation of the gods the venerable Brahmā replied as follows to the gods, who were greatly alarmed, and had been thrown into confusion by the might of the sons of Sagara, who had brought about the destruction of living beings on a large scale : (1)

verses.text:
यस्येयं वसुधा कृत्स्ना वासुदेवस्य धीमतः।
महिषी माधवस्यैषा स एव भगवान् प्रभुः॥ २॥
कापिलं रूपमास्थाय धारयत्यनिशं धराम्।
तस्य कोपाग्निना दग्धा भविष्यन्ति नृपात्मजाः॥ ३॥
verses.m: “This Goddess Earth is a Consort of the all-wise Lord Viṣṇu, the Spouse of Lakṣmī, the goddess of fortune, to whom this entire globe belongs. Assuming the form of Kapila the same almighty Lord incessantly supports the earth by dint of His yogic power. The sons of Sagara will be shortly consumed by the fire of His wrath. (2-3)

verses.text:
पृथिव्याश्चापि निर्भेदो दृष्ट एव सतानतः।
सगरस्य च पुत्राणां विनाशो दीर्घदर्शिनाम्॥ ४॥
verses.m: “The excavation of the earth invariably takes place in every Kalpa. And the destruction of the sons of Sagara too is foreseen by men possessing a long range of vision. Hence there is no occasion for grief on this account either.” (4)

verses.text:
पितामहवचः श्रुत्वा त्रयस्त्रिंशदरिंदमाः।
देवाः परमसंहृष्टाः पुनर्जग्मुर्यथागतम्॥ ५॥
verses.m: Hearing the reply of Brahmā, the progenitor of the entire creation, the gods, thirty-three* in number, all capable of subduing their enemy, returned extremely delighted to their respective abode the way they had come. (5)

verses.text:
सगरस्य च पुत्राणां प्रादुरासीन्महास्वनः।
पृथिव्यां भिद्यमानायां निर्घातसमनिःस्वनः॥ ६॥
verses.m: And while the earth was being excavated at the hands of Sagara’s sons, there arose a terrific sound like that of a thunderstorm. (6)

verses.text:
ततो भित्त्वा महीं सर्वां कृत्वा चापि प्रदक्षिणम्।
सहिताः सागराः सर्वे पितरं वाक्यमब्रुवन्॥ ७॥
verses.m: Having walked round the whole earth and excavated it too, all the sons of Sagara then sought the presence of their father and jointly made the following submission to him : (7)

verses.text:
परिक्रान्ता मही सर्वा सत्त्ववन्तश्च सूदिताः।
देवदानवरक्षांसि पिशाचोरगपन्नगाः॥ ८॥
verses.m: “The entire globe has been circumambulated and excavated and powerful gods, demons and ogres, fiends, serpents and Nāgas destroyed by us. (8)

verses.text:
न च पश्यामहेऽश्वं ते अश्वहर्तारमेव च।
किं करिष्याम भद्रं ते बुद्धिरत्र विचार्यताम्॥ ९॥
verses.m: “Yet we have neither been able to trace the horse nor the stealer of the horse. What shall we do now? May your benign look descend on us and let a further plan of action be thought out for us in this matter.” (9)

verses.text:
तेषां तद् वचनं श्रुत्वा पुत्राणां राजसत्तमः।
समन्युरब्रवीद् वाक्यं सगरो रघुनन्दन॥ १०॥
verses.m: Hearing the aforesaid submission of those princes, O scion of Raghu, Sagara, the noblest of kings, angrily replied as follows: (10)

verses.text:
भूयः खनत भद्रं वो विभेद्य वसुधातलम्।
अश्वहर्तारमासाद्य कृतार्थाश्च निवर्तत॥ ११॥
verses.m: “May prosperity attend you, excavate the earth further and, breaking it open, trace the stealer of the horse and return only when you have accomplished your purpose.” (11)

verses.text:
पितुर्वचनमासाद्य सगरस्य महात्मनः।
षष्टिः पुत्रसहस्राणि रसातलमभिद्रवन्॥ १२॥
verses.m: Bowing to the command of their high-souled father, Sagara, the sixty thousand princes dug their way into Rasātala. (12)

verses.text:
खन्यमाने ततस्तस्मिन् ददृशुः पर्वतोपमम्।
दिशागजं विरूपाक्षं धारयन्तं महीतलम्॥ १३॥
verses.m: Even while the earth was being further tunnelled, they saw as a sequel to that excavation an elephant huge as a mountain, Virūpākṣa by name, guarding the eastern quarter and supporting the globe. (13)

verses.text:
सपर्वतवनां कृत्स्नां पृथिवीं रघुनन्दन।
धारयामास शिरसा विरूपाक्षो महागजः॥ १४॥
verses.m: The great elephant Virūpākṣa, O scion of Raghu, supported on his head the entire globe including the mountains and forests. (14)

verses.text:
यदा पर्वणि काकुत्स्थ विश्रमार्थं महागजः।
खेदाच्चालयते शीर्षं भूमिकम्पस्तदा भवेत्॥ १५॥
verses.m: Whenever, from exhaustion, O scion of Kakutstha, the great elephant shakes his head for the sake of relief, a convulsion of the earth’s surface ensues. (15)

verses.text:
ते तं प्रदक्षिणं कृत्वा दिशापालं महागजम्।
मानयन्तो हि ते राम जग्मुर्भित्त्वा रसातलम्॥ १६॥
verses.m: Walking clockwise round that great elephant guarding the quarter, and thereby showing their respect to him, O Rāma, they tunnelled their way through Rasātala indeed. (16)

verses.text:
ततः पूर्वां दिशं भित्त्वा दक्षिणां बिभिदुः पुनः।
दक्षिणस्यामपि दिशि ददृशुस्ते महागजम्॥ १७॥
महापद्मं महात्मानं सुमहत्पर्वतोपमम्।
शिरसा धारयन्तं गां विस्मयं जग्मुरुत्तमम्॥ १८॥
verses.m: Having pierced the eastern quarter they then penetrated the southern quarter too, and in the southern quarter again they found the great elephant, Mahāpadma, endowed with a colossal body resembling a huge mountain and supporting the earth on his head, and experienced great wonder. (17-18)

verses.text:
ते तं प्रदक्षिणं कृत्वा सगरस्य महात्मनः।
षष्टिः पुत्रसहस्राणि पश्चिमां बिभिदुर्दिशम्॥ १९॥
verses.m: Walking round the elephant from left to right as a mark of respect, the sixty thousand sons of the high-souled Sagara penetrated the western quarter. (19)

verses.text:
पश्चिमायामपि दिशि महान्तमचलोपमम्।
दिशागजं सौमनसं ददृशुस्ते महाबलाः॥ २०॥
verses.m: In the western quarter too those very mighty princes beheld the great elephant guarding that quarter, Saumanasa by name, that resembled a mountain in size. (20)

verses.text:
ते तं प्रदक्षिणं कृत्वा पृष्ट्वा चापि निरामयम्।
खनन्तः समुपाक्रान्ता दिशं सोमवतीं तदा॥ २१॥
verses.m: Walking round the elephant clockwise and enquiring after his welfare, they then dug their way into the northern quarter, presided over by the moon-god. (21)

verses.text:
उत्तरस्यां रघुश्रेष्ठ ददृशुर्हिमपाण्डुरम्।
भद्रं भद्रेण वपुषा धारयन्तं महीमिमाम्॥ २२॥
verses.m: In the north, O chief of the Raghus, they saw Bhadra, the elephant guarding that quarter, white as snow, supporting this globe on his beautiful body. (22)

verses.text:
समालभ्य ततः सर्वे कृत्वा चैनं प्रदक्षिणम्।
षष्टिः पुत्रसहस्राणिं बिभिदुर्वसुधातलम्॥ २३॥
verses.m: Touching the elephant and walking round him from left to right, all the sixty thousand princes set about digging the earth once more. (23)

verses.text:
ततः प्रागुत्तरां गत्वा सागराः प्रथितां दिशम्।
रोषादभ्यखनन् सर्वे पृथिवीं सगरात्मजाः॥ २४॥
verses.m: Proceeding in the celebrated north-easterly direction, presided over by Lord Śiva and as such held sacred for all holy undertakings, all the sons of Sagara continued digging the earth in an agitated mood. (24)

verses.text:
ते तु सर्वे महात्मानो भीमवेगा महाबलाः।
ददृशुः कपिलं तत्र वासुदेवं सनातनम्॥ २५॥
हयं च तस्य देवस्य चरन्तमविदूरतः।
प्रहर्षमतुलं प्राप्ताः सर्वे ते रघुनन्दन॥ २६॥
verses.m: All those high-minded and exceedingly mighty princes, possessed of tremendous speed, actually beheld there the eternal Lord Viṣṇu manifested in the form of Sage Kapila, as well as a horse grazing not very far from that glorious sage, on which they all experienced incomparable joy, O scion of Raghu ! (25-26)

verses.text:
ते तं यज्ञहनं ज्ञात्वा क्रोधपर्याकुलेक्षणाः।
खनित्रलाङ्गलधरा नानावृक्षशिलाधराः॥ २७॥
अभ्यधावन्त संक्रुद्धास्तिष्ठ तिष्ठेति चाब्रुवन्।
अस्माकं त्वं हि तुरगं यज्ञियं हृतवानसि॥ २८॥
verses.m: Thoughtlessly suspecting him to be the man who had interrupted the sacrificial performance by stealing away the sacrificial horse, they felt enraged and rushed towards him with their eyes bedimmed through anger, carrying spades and ploughs and various kinds of trees and rocks, and said, “Stop ! Stop !! You alone have stolen our sacrificial horse. (27-28)

verses.text:
दुर्मेधस्त्वं हि सम्प्राप्तान् विद्धि नः सगरात्मजान्।
श्रुत्वा तद् वचनं तेषां कपिलो रघुनन्दन॥ २९॥
रोषेण महताऽऽविष्टो हुंकारमकरोत् तदा।
ततस्तेनाप्रमेयेण कपिलेन महात्मना।
भस्मराशीकृताः सर्वे काकुत्स्थ सगरात्मजाः॥ ३०॥
verses.m: “Indeed, you know us to be the sons of Sagara arrived in a body, O evil-minded one !” Seized with fury to hear that threat of theirs, O scion of Raghu, Kapila forthwith uttered the sound ‘hum’, expressive of contempt. The very next moment the sons of Sagara were all burnt and reduced to a heap of ashes by that high-souled Sage Kapila of immeasurable glory. (29-30)

verses.text:
पुत्रांश्चिरगताञ्ज्ञात्वा सगरो रघुनन्दन।
नप्तारमब्रवीद् राजा दीप्यमानं स्वतेजसा॥ १॥
verses.m: Perceiving that his sons had been away for a long time, O scion of Raghu, King Sagara spoke as follows to his grandson, Aṁśumān, resplendent with his own glory : (1)

verses.text:
शूरश्च कृतविद्यश्च पूर्वैस्तुल्योऽसि तेजसा।
पितॄणां गतिमन्विच्छ येन चाश्वोऽपवाहितः॥ २॥
verses.m: “You are valiant and learned and the compeer of your forbears in splendour. Trace the whereabouts of your uncles as well as of the man by whom the sacrificial horse has been stolen away. (2)

verses.text:
अन्तर्भौमानि सत्त्वानि वीर्यवन्ति महान्ति च।
तेषां तु प्रतिघातार्थं सासिं गृह्णीष्व कार्मुकम्॥ ३॥
verses.m: “The living beings inhabiting the subterranean regions are full of great prowess and gigantic of body. In order to meet their assault, therefore, take up a bow alongwith a sword. (3)

verses.text:
अभिवाद्याभिवाद्यांस्त्वं हत्वा विघ्नकरानपि।
सिद्धार्थः संनिवर्तस्व मम यज्ञस्य पारगः॥ ४॥
verses.m: “Bowing to those who deserve to be greeted and at the same time killing those who come in your way, return you only when you have accomplished your purpose, and thus ensure the completion of my sacrificial performance.” (4)

verses.text:
एवमुक्तोंऽशुमान् सम्यक् सगरेण महात्मना।
धनुरादाय खड्गं च जगाम लघुविक्रमः॥ ५॥
verses.m: Duly instructed thus by the high-souled Sagara and taking his bow and sword, Aṁśumān departed with quick paces. (5)

verses.text:
स खातं पितृभिर्मार्गमन्तर्भौमं महात्मभिः।
प्रापद्यत नरश्रेष्ठ तेन राज्ञाभिचोदितः॥ ६॥
verses.m: Urged by the aforesaid king, O jewel among men, he reached in no time the underground passage dug by his high-minded uncles. (6)

verses.text:
देवदानवरक्षोभिः पिशाचपतगोरगैः।
पूज्यमानं महातेजा दिशागजमपश्यत॥ ७॥
verses.m: The exceptionally glorious Aṁśumān presently saw an elephant guarding one of the four quarters, that was being worshipped by gods, demons and ogres, fiends, winged creatures and serpents. (7)

verses.text:
स तं प्रदक्षिणं कृत्वा पृष्ट्वा चैव निरामयम्।
पितॄन् स परिपप्रच्छ वाजिहर्तारमेव च॥ ८॥
verses.m: Walking clockwise round the elephant and inquiring after his welfare, he questioned him about his uncles as well as about the stealer of the sacrificial horse of his father. (8)

verses.text:
दिशागजस्तु तच्छ्रुत्वा प्रत्युवाच महामतिः।
आसमञ्ज कृतार्थस्त्वं सहाश्वः शीघ्रमेष्यसि॥ ९॥
verses.m: Hearing his aforesaid question, the highly intelligent elephant presiding over the quarter, for his part, replied, “Accomplished of purpose, O son of Asamañja, you will soon come back alongwith the horse.” (9)

verses.text:
तस्य तद् वचनं श्रुत्वा सर्वानेव दिशागजान्।
यथाक्रमं यथान्यायं प्रष्टुं समुपचक्रमे॥ १०॥
verses.m: Hearing the aforesaid reply of the elephant, Aṁśumān proceeded to ask the same question of all the elephants guarding the quarters in their order of seniority and in a befitting manner. (10)

verses.text:
तैश्च सर्वैर्दिशापालैर्वाक्यज्ञैर्वाक्यकोविदैः।
पूजितः सहयश्चैवागन्तासीत्यभिचोदितः॥ ११॥
verses.m: He was received with honour by all the elephants guarding all the four quarters—who could easily understand the meaning of others’ speech and were equally adept in expression—and told that he would return alongwith the horse. (11)

verses.text:
तेषां तद् वचनं श्रुत्वा जगाम लघुविक्रमः।
भस्मराशीकृता यत्र पितरस्तस्य सागराः॥ १२॥
verses.m: Hearing that reply of theirs, Aṁśumān repaired with quick paces to the place where his uncles, the sons of Sagara, lay reduced to heaps of ashes. (12)

verses.text:
स दुःखवशमापन्नस्त्वसमञ्जसुतस्तदा।
चुक्रोश परमार्तस्तु वधात् तेषां सुदुःखितः॥ १३॥
verses.m: Already fallen a prey to affliction on not finding them, the said son of Asamañja for his part thereupon felt deeply distressed over their death and actually cried in great agony. (13)

verses.text:
यज्ञियं च हयं तत्र चरन्तमविदूरतः।
ददर्श पुरुषव्याघ्रो दुःखशोकसमन्वितः॥ १४॥
verses.m: Nay, full of sorrow and grief the tiger among men also perceived the sacrificial horse grazing on the spot not very far from him. (14)

verses.text:
स तेषां राजपुत्राणां कर्तुकामो जलक्रियाम्।
स जलार्थी महातेजा न चापश्यज्जलाशयम्॥ १५॥
verses.m: He felt inclined to offer water to the spirits of those princes. Though desirous of water for that purpose, that exceptionally glorious prince, however, did not come across any reservoir of water nearby. (15)

verses.text:
विसार्य निपुणां दृष्टिं ततोऽपश्यत् खगाधिपम्।
पितॄणां मातुलं राम सुपर्णमनिलोपम्॥ १६॥
verses.m: Extending his penetrating vision all round, O Rāma, he then saw Garuḍa, the king of birds, who is swift as the wind, and the maternal uncle of his uncles. (16)

verses.text:
स चैनमब्रवीद् वाक्यं वैनतेयो महाबलः।
मा शुचः पुरुषव्याघ्र वधोऽयं लोकसम्मतः॥ १७॥
कपिलेनाप्रमेयेण दग्धा हीमे महाबलाः।
सलिलं नार्हसि प्राज्ञ दातुमेषां हि लौकिकम्॥ १८॥
verses.m: The exceptionally mighty Garuḍa (son of Vinatā), however, addressed to him the following admonition : “This death of your uncles, O tiger among men, is conducive to the interests of all the three worlds inasmuch as it will serve as an occasion for the advent of the holy Gaṅgā to the terrestrial plane. These exceptionally mighty princes have undoubtedly been burnt to death by Sage Kapila of immeasurable glory. You should not therefore offer them earthly* water, O wise prince ! (17-18)

verses.text:
गङ्गा हिमवतो ज्येष्ठा दुहिता पुरुषर्षभ।
तस्यां कुरु महाबाहो पितॄणां सलिलक्रियाम्॥ १९॥
verses.m: Gaṅgā is the elder daughter of Himavān, the deity presiding over the Himālayas. Offer water, O mighty-armed prince, to the soul of your departed uncles in that river, O jewel among men ! (19)

verses.text:
भस्मराशीकृतानेतान् प्लावयेल्लोकपावनी।
तया क्लिन्नमिदं भस्म गङ्गया लोककान्तया।
षष्टिं पुत्रसहस्राणि स्वर्गलोकं गमिष्यति॥ २०॥
verses.m: “When the Gaṅgā, which is capable of purifying the whole world, washes them, reduced as they are to heaps of ashes, this heap of ashes soaked by the Gaṅgā, a river pleasing to the world, will take the souls of the sixty thousand princes to the celestial plane. (20)

verses.text:
निर्गच्छाश्वं महाभाग संगृह्य पुरुषर्षभ।
यज्ञं पैतामहं वीर निर्वर्तयितुमर्हसि॥ २१॥
verses.m: “Taking the horse with you, O highly blessed one, depart from this region, O jewel among men ! Thereby you ought to ensure the completion of your grandfather’s sacrificial undertaking, O valiant prince !” (21)

verses.text:
सुपर्णवचनं श्रुत्वा सोंऽशुमानतिवीर्यवान्।
त्वरितं हयमादाय पुनरायान्महातपाः॥ २२॥
verses.m: Hearing the admonition of Garuḍa, the celebrated Aṁśumān, who was exceptionally powerful and a great ascetic too, speedily returned to his grandfather’s capital taking the sacrificial horse with him. (22)

verses.text:
ततो राजानमासाद्य दीक्षितं रघुनन्दन।
न्यवेदयद् यथा वृत्तं सुपर्णवचनं तथा॥ २३॥
verses.m: Then seeking the presence of the king, who stood consecrated for the sacrifice yet, O scion of Raghu, he related exactly what had happened as well as reproduced faithfully the utterance of Garuḍa. (23)

verses.text:
तच्छ्रुत्वा घोरसंकाशं वाक्यमंशुमतो नृपः।
यज्ञं निर्वर्तयामास यथाकल्पं यथाविधि॥ २४॥
verses.m: Hearing that apparently awe-inspiring tale from the lips of Aṁśumān, the king Sagara concluded the sacrifice to the best of his capacity in accordance with the scriptural ordinance. (24)

verses.text:
स्वपुरं त्वगमच्छ्रीमानिष्टयज्ञो महीपतिः।
गङ्गायाश्चागमे राजा निश्चयं नाध्यगच्छत॥ २५॥
verses.m: Having performed the sacrifice the glorious emperor for his part returned to his capital. The monarch, however, could not hit upon any plan for ensuring the descent of the Gaṅgā to the terrestrial plane. (25)

verses.text:
अगत्वा निश्चयं राजा कालेन महता महान्।
त्रिंशद्वर्षसहस्राणि राज्यं कृत्वा दिवं गतः॥ २६॥
verses.m: Failing to reach any conclusion in the aforesaid matter even after a considerable time and having reigned for thirty thousand years, the great king ascended to heaven. (26)

verses.text:
कालधर्मं गते राम सगरे प्रकृतीजनाः।
राजानं रोचयामासुरंशुमन्तं सुधार्मिकम्॥ १॥
verses.m: Sagara having met his end (which is the law of Time, according to which one who is born must die sooner or later when one has played one’s allotted role), O Rāma, the people desired the highly pious Aṁśumān to be their ruler. (1)

verses.text:
स राजा सुमहानासीदंशुमान् रघुनन्दन।
तस्य पुत्रो महानासीद् दिलीप इति विश्रुतः॥ २॥
verses.m: The said Aṁśumān, O scion of Raghu, proved to be a great monarch. His son, widely known by the name of Dilīpa, was equally great. (2)

verses.text:
तस्मै राज्यं समादिश्य दिलीपे रघुनन्दन।
हिमवच्छिखरे रम्ये तपस्तेपे सुदारुणम्॥ ३॥
verses.m: Having entrusted the kingship to the said Dilīpa, O scion of Raghu, Aṁśumān practised the severest form of askesis (for bringing down the Gaṅgā to the terrestrial plane) on a delightful summit of the Himālayas. (3)

verses.text:
द्वात्रिंशच्छतसाहस्रं वर्षाणि सुमहायशाः।
तपोवनगतो राजा स्वर्गं लेभे तपोधनः॥ ४॥
verses.m: Having continued for thirty-two lakhs of years in a grove intended for austerities alone, the highly illustrious king, rich in asceticism, eventually attained heaven only and not the desired grace of the holy Gaṅgā. (4)

verses.text:
दिलीपस्तु महातेजाः श्रुत्वा पैतामहं वधम्।
दुःखोपहतया बुद्ध्या निश्चयं नाध्यगच्छत॥ ५॥
verses.m: Hearing of the unnatural death of his grand-uncles, the exceptionally glorious Dilīpa could not arrive at any decision regarding the method of bringing the Gaṅgā down to the terrestrial plane due to his judgment being clouded by sorrow. (5)

verses.text:
कथं गङ्गावतरणं कथं तेषां जलक्रिया।
तारयेयं कथं चैतानिति चिन्तापरोऽभवत्॥ ६॥
verses.m: He felt anxious as to how the Gaṅgā should be made to descend to the terrestrial plane, how water could be offered to them and as to how he should be able to redeem their departed souls. (6)

verses.text:
